Recognize isosceles triangles and calculate missing angles, equal side lengths, and perimeter.
An isosceles triangle has at least two equal sides; the angles opposite those equal sides are equal.
The two equal sides are legs. The third side is the base. The angle between legs is the vertex angle; the other two are base angles.
For AB=AC, ∠B=∠C. Vertex angle = 180° − 2(base angle); base angle = (180° − vertex angle)/2.
